headline: Cell-type networks and donor-aware models tie molecular programs to disease outcomes
label: Cell Type Aware Disease Modeling
summary: TriSCOPE, SPIN and network-guided plasma proteomics apply cell-type and network-level models to population cohorts for disease attribution and prediction.
synthesis: The dominant thread is using cell-type-resolved or network-structured molecular models to attribute disease and clinical outcomes across many individuals. TriSCOPE combines multivariate predictive modeling, donor-aware differential expression and pseudotime across ~4.2M nuclei from 627 donors to resolve genetically anchored, cell-type-specific Alzheimer's programs. SPIN integrates spatially informed cell-type co-expression networks with Bayesian regression for population-scale clinical prediction and biological discovery. At the plasma level, a network-guided framework links HDBA and UK Biobank proteomics to compact protein panels evaluated across 23 diseases. SEMPER supplies a cell-type-specific resource, aligning protein language model embeddings with interaction networks from 442 adult human brain cell types for zero-shot inference. scMINA addresses interpretability in paired scRNA-scATAC multiome data through covariate correction and XAI-based regulatory prioritization. The shared emphasis is moving from cell-level description toward structured, interpretable models that connect cell types, networks and donor-level phenotypes, though only TriSCOPE explicitly models donor structure in differential testing.
